i express my support for the protection of minorities, respect for their culture, languages, traditions and customs. i believe that all member states should include in their national legislation, in various fields, specifications relating to the protection of minorities. in this respect, i believe that romania has a particularly well-constructed legislation in this area and can serve as an example for the other member states. the fact that the hungarian people are not the only ones who are suffering from the effects of the war in bosnia and herzegovina, and that the hungarian people are not the only ones who are suffering from the effects of the war in bosnia, is a fact which is not to be denied. the protection of minorities must not, however, lead to exaggerations such as collective rights, the promotion of autonomy and self-determination, including territorial ones. i also don't think it's helpful to divide minorities into different categories, because it can lead to the idea that different treatments are needed for these categories. all citizens must be treated equally, must have the same rights and obligations to the communities in which they live. decentralisation and local autonomy within national laws respond very well to all the wishes of citizens, regardless of nationality or ethnicity. it is not right to bring into question concepts which are not yet enshrined in current international law and which are not accepted at the level of the states and there is no need to take up council of europe provisions. a special mention should be made of the roma minority. i strongly believe that joint programmes at union level, especially in the field of education, would substantially accelerate the integration of roma. finally, i would remind you that any nation, however large, is a minority compared with the 500 million citizens of europe.
at european level there is a consistent set of rules, criteria and recommendations that ensure the protection of citizens belonging to national minorities and cases of violation of these are quite rare within the european union. romania has recognised rights for national minorities that go beyond european standards in this area, and the presence of romanian parliamentarians of hungarian nationality in this forum is living proof of this. it is essential for inter-ethnic harmony in europe that human rights be respected, but separatist excesses based on the exacerbation of ethnic rights must be stopped. the european project is one of integration, not enclaves on ethnic grounds. i also believe that we should pay more attention to the situation of national minorities in the countries neighbouring the union, especially when it comes to citizens of the same nationality as some of the member states. an example is the romanians in ukraine, serbia and the republic of moldova, deprived of basic rights and subject to an intense process of denationalization.
mr president, i welcome this debate, the more so as european history shows that in times of crisis ethnic tensions can inflame otherwise stable situations. i would like to believe that the intent of the initiators of this debate is to emphasise the generous core values and realities of the european project, because the realities of the european union are indeed the best standards in the world for the treatment of minorities. therefore, we should say out loud that this assembly does not and will not accept any divisive actions or the lowering of the standards i have just mentioned. as commissioner barrot has underlined, in each individual country of the union, there is a clear and, more often than not, official legal framework that ensures the protection of our cultural diversity. yet, for the sustainability of our multi-ethnic society, is there any alternative to higher education? real-life examples show that solving issues related to education fuels strong community development. education is, by its own nature, unifying rather than divisive. in fact, it teaches us that we are all someone else’s minority. the babeş-bolyai university in romania, in the transylvanian city of cluj, is an example of a multicultural university that has been cited time and again by the organisation for security and cooperation in europe as a positive example of multicultural and inter-ethnic excellence. where the need arises, higher-degree education in the language of minorities is part of the national educational system. let me give you the example of sapientia university in romania. these positive examples, however, do not mean that we can take our eye off the ball, and we must be aware that maybe the most challenging issue lies ahead of us: solving the difficult situation of the roma community throughout europe. it is my belief that the most effective way of solving this tremendously difficult european problem in the long term is through education. i would very much like to see a very substantial debate on how europe intends to take advantage of our unique educational system, so that we remain united in our diversity.
the council of europe is the institution that deals with the respect of human rights. the rights and protection of minorities fall within the competence of the member states, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity. traditional and ethnic minorities, migrant minorities and immigrants must respect the national legislation of the member state of residence. i believe that the integration of the new migrant minorities should not be part of the common immigration policy currently being drawn up by the union. this policy can only be defined when the existing barriers to the free movement of workers from the member states which joined the european union after 2004 disappear within the union. the protection of migrant minorities is one of the principles promoted by social europe. ensuring fair working conditions for all european citizens, regardless of their member state of origin, guarantees them a decent life. as a european socialist, i support the development of a european framework for legal immigration but i militate first and foremost for the respect of the basic principles of the european union for all european citizens.
unfortunately, this draft resolution is only before parliament today in the form of a question. representatives of traditional national minorities, communities, are trying to convince the majority, through peaceful means, through parliamentary means, that what is good in the 14 countries of europe will be good in the whole of the union. traditional national minorities have moved to a new country through no fault of their own, without ever having left their centuries-old homes. no one asked them if they wanted to change their citizenship, to learn a new official language. these traditional national minorities are the most loyal citizens of their countries. despite wars, economic crises, internal political battles, assimilation, they have not left their native homelands, old and new. their loyalty is unwavering. that is why it is incomprehensible that tens of millions of people in large countries are afraid of a few hundred thousand, perhaps half a million, one and a half million minorities. the various forms of self-determination used in the union, such as territorial or cultural autonomy, which is the result of a consensus policy of the majority and the minority, have not weakened the economic, political and social strength of the country concerned, or even that of the european union. my country, romania, has existed in its present form since 1920. in this area, 28% of the non-romanian population lived in 1930, today this number has decreased to 10%. several member states, including romania, have similar problems. there are laws, rights, but they cannot guarantee the implementation of these, even though linguistic, ethnic, regional diversity is a european value. it is therefore important that the existing and well-established eu models should be used to develop a guiding principle that is acceptable to all and does not infringe the territorial integrity of the countries.
firstly, i do not believe that the european union needs a common policy on minorities; we owe equal rights to all european citizens, regardless of ethnicity. on the other hand, if the signatories of the question under debate want a european policy in this respect, we assure them that, for example, romanian legislation can be considered an example of good practice. romania has perhaps the most generous and modern legislation at european level on national minorities. they enjoy broad political and social rights, identical to those of all citizens; significant minorities, such as the hungarian minority, receive education in their mother tongue at all levels; representatives of minorities have the right to seats in parliament, even if they do not obtain the necessary votes. moreover, the party of the hungarian minority which was invoked this evening and in the debates last night, has been part of the romanian government for 12 of the 19 years that romania has functioned as a democratic state.
minorities of all kinds must be supported both in preserving their own identity, values, traditions and language, and in developing their culture. in my view, romania, as a unitary and sovereign state, is a model in respecting the individual rights of members of any minority. i appreciate the approach of my fellow members of parliament and their continuing concern for the protection of ethnic, traditional or national minorities. it is a natural and welcome thing. but as far as the majority-minority connection goes, i want to make two points clear: 1) i believe that not only members of a minority should be involved in such actions, but also, to the same extent, the majority should be concerned about issues related to minorities, precisely to support and protect what we call "unity in diversity", which is happening in romania, and 2) i believe that, to the same extent, minorities should also be concerned about the state of the majority, because these two entities form, only together, that whole unit that contributes to the natural development of any society.
in the context of this debate, i would like to make a point to point out that national minorities make a lot of noise because they do not have arguments for all the rights they claim. i would like to launch a phrase in this regard, namely: "noise does no good and good does not make much noise". the european union's laws cannot only protect minorities and disadvantage national communities, because we are facing positive discrimination. i'd like to give an example where reality disproves what some people say. some have claimed that the rights of hungarian minorities are not respected in the field of education in romania, and since they come from the field of education, i would like to give an example that universities in romania have european standards in the field of treatment of minorities.
in the context of this debate, i would like to highlight the deterioration of the respect for the religious rights of romanians in the timoc valley, serbia. we're talking about a community of over 100,000 romanians. i hereby express my concern at the decision of the mayor of negotin, serbia, to demolish the foundation of the romanian-speaking orthodox church, although the priest boian alexandru has obtained all the necessary approvals. this church would be the second for romanians living in serbia. for the courage to build the first, priest boian alexander was sentenced to two months suspended. i would stress that serbia has committed itself, in accordance with article 5 of the stabilisation and association agreement, to respect human rights and the protection of ethnic and religious minorities. i would like to end with a quote from a letter by the priest boian alexandru, in the hope that the serbian authorities will not demolish this church where they will worship in romanian. i quote: ... to help us to acquire these rights in our country where we live, serbia, to have at least our church and school and to be able to speak romanian.
mr president, the european union has no jurisdiction as far as the status of national minorities in the member states is concerned. there is no problem, however, because all european union member states are also members of the council of europe, an organisation which is well-equipped and well-experienced to address that issue. to duplicate the activity of the council of europe would be detrimental to the scope of our work on minorities and would only create confusion and frustration. secondly, i am concerned to see that our approach on minorities places too much emphasis on solutions that were perhaps valid decades and centuries ago. i believe that in this field, as well, it would be better to develop our imagination more than our memory. finally, instead of revisiting fields already explored, the european union would be better advised to develop a concept of transnational protection of cultural rights in a continent where each ethno-cultural community is a minority as well.
in the current global context of globalisation and the mobility of people, i think that what has been said here tonight about territorial authority is meaningless. i think there are over a million romanians in spain and italy and i don't see why they would want territorial autonomy in those countries. i think that the creation of a committee or subcommittee at the european parliament level for the observance of minority rights would be a very good idea and would put into practice a european policy at this level, or, finally, if you wish, certain procedures for the observance of minority rights. i don't think romania has ever refused a visit from a president of any european state, which is what happened here. i think romania is an example of good practice for many of the countries of the european union.
thank you very much, mr. president. national minorities living in the european union enrich the union. the european parliament should take the lead in protecting ethnic minorities by initiating a meaningful debate on the legal status of minorities. parliament should undertake to develop and adopt a framework of rules which are binding on all member states. this framework is in fact in the interests of minority communities if it includes in its provisions, taking into account the principle of subsidiarity, that the implementation of different forms of autonomy based on consensus between the majority and the minority is the best way to ensure the appropriate status of minority communities. thank you, sir.
in writing. mr president,ladies and gentlemen,i come from a region on the romanian-hungarian border, in the county of arad, where the problems of minorities have long been overcome. here, colleagues and childhood friends who attended primary school and then university studies in hungarian, today also use hungarian in the institutions where they work. i ruled arad county and the western region of romania. in this area, in the counties of arad, timis and bihor in romania, and csongrad and bekes in hungary, romanians together with hungarians have completed dozens of joint projects and are continuing others, using a single, european language to solve common european problems. i invite all those who wish to know the romanian model of solving the minority problem on the spot, before expressing themselves in various european forums, to know the reality on the spot.
the report presents both scientific data and recommendations for combating climate change, addressing both adaptation and reducing the causes that lead to it. fighting climate change is not only an obligation to ensure the future of future generations, but also an opportunity to revive the global economy. i ask that the importance of energy efficiency be reflected in the community budget and in the financial instruments available. making transport more efficient through the use of intelligent transport systems, promoting rail and shipping, ensuring intermodality and investing in greener cars will reduce emissions from this sector. i have recommended the development of greener types of tourism, such as sports tourism or cultural tourism, and i stress that the best tourist destinations should be those that respect and protect the environment. i think that an international fund should be considered to plant trees on unused land. in conclusion, he said that research is needed in medical science and pharmaceuticals to produce drugs and vaccines that will be available to all people affected by certain diseases at an affordable price.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, in the last few months we have seen what it means for the global economy to be hit by an unprecedented crisis, the credit crisis. but the climate, food and social crises are also being felt. in romania, we have been facing declines in production in recent years due to external causes such as floods, drought, avian influenza, to which economic problems have been added in recent months. in the context of the financial crisis, it will be increasingly difficult for us to cover from the state budget the damage caused by floods or drought. throughout my work in the committee on agriculture, i have supported the idea of setting up independent intervention mechanisms at community level, independent of the value of national ceilings. i also believe that in a confrontation of this magnitude we must prioritize investments in clean technologies and renewable energy. they are a solution to the climate crisis and at the same time, economic recovery through job creation. as part of our european mandate, we have a duty to persuade our governments to invest more in innovation and new environmental technologies.
in writing. i believe that mr florenz's report 2050: the future starts today recommendations for a future integrated policy for environmental protection in the eu was timely and necessary in view of the observed and anticipated effects of climate change. romania is one of the first european countries to sign the kyoto protocol, whereby it has committed itself to supporting the fight against climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 8% by 2012. i am convinced of the need for these measures, although, compared to many other european countries, romania has low greenhouse gas emissions. both agriculture and the romanian forestry fund can play an important role in the fight against climate change, which has been strongly felt in recent years, especially through floods and high temperatures and prolonged droughts. these phenomena affect both agricultural and forest productivity and valuable habitats and ecosystems. agriculture and forestry are expected to continue to make an important contribution to combating the effects of climate change through afforestation to absorb and retain greenhouse gases and the use of biomass as a source of renewable energy.
in writing. the european union has played a major role in the effort to find a compromise for a global post-kyoto agreement and it is possible that, together with the new us administration, a concrete way to achieve this agreement can be found. concrete measures to combat the effects of climate change offer just as many opportunities for sustainable socioeconomic development and job creation. they are particularly targeted at new and dynamic sectors with major growth potential, in which insufficient investment has been made to date. these measures, in addition to their beneficial effect in the fight against climate change, will also have a positive effect in mitigating the effects of the economic and financial crisis and may lead, in the long term, to a decrease in the european union's dependence on energy imports. we are talking about accelerated investment in transport infrastructure, renewable energy, biotechnology, waste collection and recycling, nuclear energy, thermal rehabilitation of housing. reforestation and measures to combat desertification can have dramatic results in the medium term.
in writing. the report provides a clear guide for future action in its 12 points. but to be able to act locally, nationally, regionally, globally, we need the support of well-informed citizens. according to the special eurobarometer on 'climate change' in spring 2008, some 41% of europeans feel poorly informed about the causes, consequences and ways of combating climate change. in romania, over 65% of citizens are not informed. raising awareness through education and awareness campaigns in everyday life is an essential step in this direction. the commission and the member states must finance awareness-raising campaigns among citizens, create conditions for training new careers adapted to the specific challenges of the labour market caused by structural economic changes, which are accelerated by climate change and its effects. in the context of the economic crisis, the eu needs to engage politically and financially in the key areas of supporting and developing 'clean' technologies to combat climate change, supporting cross-border adaptation measures, increasing energy efficiency and disaster relief, in line with the eu principle of solidarity. all this means creating 'green' jobs in new and competitive enterprises.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, any debate about climate, ecosystem, energy, is extremely important, because any major change in these can affect life on earth. regardless of the causes or the scientific arguments of different groups of scientists, one thing is certain: we are facing a global warming phenomenon. this comprehensive and consistent report, with all the useful and valuable information it provides, prompts the question: what can we do for ourselves and future generations? in this climate change context, i believe there are three types of projects that eu member states should develop and support as a matter of priority: 1. projects concerning the implementation of common policies for the most efficient management of energy and the search for solutions to reduce pollution, particularly in the case of industrial zones and parks. 2. projects relating to the financing of scientific research capable of developing non-polluting technologies. 3. projects that immediately support concrete actions to restore the ecosystem both at european level and in any other area of the world.
in writing. the european union has taken a leading role in the fight against climate change, and a long-term strategy for efficient management of natural resources will ensure a low-carbon global economy. this strategy must be based on the principle of solidarity in order to achieve a balance between rich countries and developing countries that need support in reducing their vulnerability to the adverse effects of climate change. global warming is translated into poverty, insufficient food and limited energy resources. it is well known that oil is no longer a sufficiently strong energy source to meet demand, which is expected to increase by at least 60% by 2030. finding alternative sources and making rational use of existing resources is a challenge facing the union in the future. agriculture is one of the sectors most exposed to climate change because of its dependence on weather conditions. given that this sector provides food for the world's population, the sustainable management of soil and water resources, as well as the protection of forests and biodiversity, will need to be on the agenda of the long-term strategy to counter the effects of global warming.
in writing. the european union has become the main actor taking concrete steps in adopting policies to respond to the global challenge of climate change. european policy in this area can become more effective globally and within the eu if: (a) european efforts are supported by those of other highly industrialized countries outside the eu, such as china, india, brazil, russia, etc.; (b) the development of nuclear energy is encouraged and not discouraged, at least for the next 30-40 years, until technologies for exploiting renewable resources are developed and costs allow for marketing without subsidies; (c) the european commission will give stronger support to energy saving and biomass energy projects, including technology transfer, in the eu's least developed and high agricultural potential member states. romania will continue to develop its nuclear electricity generation programme. it will also modernise coal-fired power stations and step up efforts to produce energy from biomass. in this respect, we need partnerships with the member states and we call for the european commission to speed up its efforts to simplify the procedures for the mobilisation of european funds.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the florenz report because i agree with the recommendations made for the future integrated environmental protection policy. this report calls on the commission to closely monitor and analyse the latest scientific research findings in order to assess, in particular, whether the eu's 2oc target would actually achieve its goal of avoiding dangerous climate change. it also stresses the importance of the eu and the other industrialised countries as a group setting a medium-term target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 25%-40% by 2020 and a long-term target of reducing emissions by at least 80% by 2050 compared to 1990, while continuing to focus on the goal of limiting the increase in average global temperature to 2oc above pre-industrial levels, thus achieving a 50% probability of achieving this target.

madam president, how many recognitions are necessary for a state to be independent? this is not the question, since the quality of the recognitions matters more than the quantity. a declaration of self-determination does not lead to independence if the state in question is not recognised by those from which it wants to self-determine. the independence of a state is not real as long as the united nations security council does not accept it. moreover, a state is not independent if it is not able to offer to all communities living on its territory a fair prospect of organic integration into a civic and multicultural society, and if it is not self-sustainable and self-governable. for all these reasons, the athisaari plan failed. asking for the status quo ante is not a solution either – one should move further. to this end, the european union and the permanent members of the united nations security council must convene an international conference which should find a sustainable solution for democratic security, geo-strategic equilibrium and social economic stability in the western balkans. within this framework kosovo should be put back on the track of international legality, and the region should receive a clear road map for its eu integration. unfortunately, the lagendijk report does not explore such ways thus abandoning any realistic drive towards a better future. therefore, romanian social democrats will be obliged to vote against this report.
in accordance with the provisions of international law and in the light of un security council resolution 1244 of 1999, kosovo cannot be considered a state. there are five eu member states that have not recognised kosovo's unilaterally declared independence. but kosovo is a reality and we must treat it as such. stability in the western balkans, the region most likely to join the union in the near future, is vital. the union must therefore play the leading role in managing the delicate situation in the area. the eulex mission, which has already reached its initial operational capability, is an important first step in this direction, as assistance and coordination are needed to ensure, first of all, a climate of inter-ethnic cooperation that will allow a return to a normal level of life. the protection of all minorities in kosovo, including the serb minority, must be ensured, institutions must be strengthened to avoid chaos and ensure stable development, property must be returned and the right of return of refugees must be guaranteed. the financial instruments at the disposal of the union, in particular the pre-accession instrument, should be used to facilitate socio-economic development, increased transparency and reconciliation between ethnic communities. kosovo must not, under any circumstances, be isolated from european processes. it must enjoy a european perspective in a regional context. we need to apply the same standards throughout the region. what is required of other countries in the region must also apply to serbia and kosovo. the european union must insist on the resumption of the dialogue between pristina and belgrade. i believe that the current form of the resolution does not reflect the full spectrum of positions of all 27 eu member states towards kosovo. the romanian delegation from the epp-de group, with the exception of the hungarian delegation, will therefore vote against this resolution.

i agree with many of the ideas expressed here, but the problem is much more complex. romania is right to consider that the legal basis for kosovo's unilateral declaration of independence is highly doubtful, since under international law minorities do not have collective rights, the right to self-determination and secession. the rights of persons belonging to national minorities are, i stress, fundamental. the secession of kosovo and the recognition of its statehood by other countries set a dangerous precedent, which was followed just a few months later by russia's unilateral recognition of the independence of the breakaway regions of south ossetia and abkhazia. in both cases, prime minister putin clearly invoked the kosovo model. separatist movements in regions such as kashmir, nagorno-karabakh, transnistria, crimea, northern cyprus, etc., immediately claimed that these regions were as entitled to independence as kosovo. i believe that in the future the european union and its member states must consistently uphold the principle of the territorial integrity of all states and actively discourage separatist tendencies. the european union must make a special effort to stabilise the entire western balkans region and to realise the european perspective.
the debate on the crisis in the automobile industry and the decisions that will follow should not be without the problems of the car component manufacturers. these have in turn been hit by the crisis as a result of the domino effect, because they depend on the beneficiaries' production interruptions. in romania, for example, there are over 400 companies producing automotive components, with a combined turnover of eur 8 billion in 2008. three quarters of these companies are small and usually produce for a single beneficiary. so i feel the effects of the crisis very hard. in such circumstances, they are forced to resort to layoffs or find solutions such as reduced hours or unpaid leave. tire manufacturers are also severely affected. given the large number of employees in these companies, i believe that it is necessary to include the manufacturers of automotive components and tires in any future formula of economic support in the context of the crisis.
in writing. if we look at the european union as a living organism, then the european automotive industry is its backbone. it represents 3% of the eu's gdp and generates a trade surplus of €35 billion. however, 2008 was a difficult year for the industry, with car sales falling in the first half of the year due to the increase in fuel prices and in the second half of the year falling by 19,3% due to the financial crisis. these are not the only difficulties facing this sector. between 2009 and 2015, the automotive sector must meet new standards for emissions, fuel economy, etc., all of which add billions of euros to the industry's costs. the above figures are also relevant because the automobile industry provides income for over 12 million families. one job at an auto company keeps four more at a supplier and five more in the related sales and marketing sectors. it is therefore clear that the health of this sector of the european economy is vital for the eu economy as a whole. in these circumstances, swift and coordinated action by governments and european institutions is absolutely necessary (programmes to return old machines in exchange for a substantial discount on the purchase of new ones, financial aid, etc.).
in writing. the economic crisis has hit the automotive industry hard, a sector that contributes significantly to the gdp of many european countries. even if the eu has no direct mechanisms to intervene, member states must be allowed to take the necessary measures to prevent the collapse of an industry on which the jobs of thousands of european citizens depend. the romanian automotive industry is also severely affected by the crisis. i am only mentioning the cases of dacia renault, which is restricting its activity, and ford, which has asked for support from the romanian state. the serious situation at european level calls for the immediate introduction of appropriate measures. i am not referring here to protective measures that distort the market, but to measures that give equal opportunities to european industry and allow workers in this industry to keep their jobs. it is not enough to act internally, we need action at european level. the economic recovery plan makes this possible by proposing new lending rules in the european banking system to facilitate access to credit. it is also important that the state aid schemes to which member states apply are quickly and easily accessible. this is a key aspect for strategic investors such as those in the automotive market.
president-in-office of the council. − let me begin by saying that i appreciate the question on smes, because during this current economic crisis the big businesses and the big companies are always strong enough to lobby for some relief, but it is much more difficult for smes and it certainly requires a systemic approach. on 1 december 2008, as you know, the council endorsed the european economic recovery plan, which was presented by the commission on 26 november 2008. as a response to the financial crisis, the council supported a stimulus which is equivalent to about 1.5% of the eu’s gross domestic product to restore business and consumer confidence. furthermore, the plan contains specific measures to support smes, the most important of which are those aimed at improving access to finance for smes and reducing the administrative burden. the council also agreed that improvements in the framework conditions for european businesses, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises, was essential to counter the effect of the crisis on competitiveness and to support and enhance job creation. the council also adopted two sets of conclusions related to providing support for smes, in the context of overall competitiveness. firstly, conclusions endorsing proposals to support smes presented in the commission communication entitled, as you probably know, ‘think small first: a small business act for europe’, this so-called sba, including an action plan outlining the priority measures requiring particular attention. secondly, conclusions from the commission communication entitled ‘towards world-class clusters in the european union – implementing the broad-based innovation strategy’. although clusters are not exclusively meant for the smes, they play an important role in many clusters that have been set up throughout the eu. at its meeting in mid-december 2008, the european council approved this european economic recovery plan and supported the full implementation of the action plan for the small business act. it has specifically supported an increase in the intervention by the european investment bank to the tune of eur 30 billion for the years 2009-2010, especially for loans to smes, which amount to an increase of eur 10 million over the eib usual lending in this sector. the council also supported a temporary exemption for two years beyond the de minimis threshold for state aid in respect of an amount of up to eur 50 000 and the adaptation of the state aid framework as required to increase support for enterprises, especially the smes. the council also called for the use of accelerated procedures for awarding public contracts provided for ec legislation, as well as for reducing the administrative burden on businesses. the czech presidency will continue to pursue this effort, because our economy is broadly based on smes, so we have our own experience with that. therefore, both of the forthcoming competitiveness councils under the czech presidency – one will take place very soon in early march, as well as the informal one which will take place in prague – will tackle the question of reducing the administrative burden, since we believe that better regulation is an important factor for improving competitiveness, in particular for smes, and it plays an even more important role in times of economic crisis. moreover, the presidency will try to make progress in the implementation of the action plan and put this sme policy at the forefront of society as well as linking the implementation of the action plan to the national reform programmes of all the member states. the presidency will also continue with the increased effort of discussing legislative proposals related to smes, such as the regulation on the statute for a european private company, which would offer smes a form of business enabling them to take advantage of their potential and develop cross-border activities. another legislative proposal i should mention is the proposed directive for reduced vat rates for labour-intensive services, which will be discussed at the upcoming ecofin councils. in addition, the council will be concerned with the review of the late payment directive, which is now being prepared and which is to ensure that small and medium-sized enterprises are paid in time for all business transactions. again, that is pretty important in the current situation.

mr president, the report on nato’s role in the eu’s security architecture reflected different approaches in the european parliament between, on the one hand, opinions which continue to look at nato as the organisation offering the strongest security guarantee to its members, and opinions which, on the contrary, see less and less need for nato in a world in which apparently there are no major threats – at least not comparable to the former soviet one. however, until now there was no member in both organisations willing to give up the nato security guarantee, even if the eu is putting weight behind its defence and security effort and has introduced its equivalent of article 5 of the washington treaty: the solidarity clause in the lisbon treaty. to my mind, the relationship between nato and the eu – the most important component of the larger transatlantic relationship – should be one that is naturally complementary and mutually advantageous to two partners who are compelled to work together in responding to today’s multiplying and increasingly complex challenges. to that effect, existing mechanisms – see the berlin plus agreements – could be improved; new ones – see the proposal for an eu operational headquarters – should be contemplated; obstacles – see the negative impact of the cyprus problem – should be overcome; and, most important, mutual perceptions should be definitely improved. thus, on the one hand, one should stop considering nato as an adversary and, on the other, the eu as an appendix to nato. as mentioned, the truth is that in practice the two partners could very well cooperate with each other, mutually complementing one another. for that, the report has been amended and hopefully the end result has become acceptable to many of us.
madam president, i want to make two points. firstly, on values. the european union is a union of values. these values are criteria for accession. they guide us in our behaviour. they are a means to build interoperability with our external partners. but we should not make the scope of our external policy from exporting our values. on the contrary, we have to learn to operate in a diversified world and even to respect the other’s right to be wrong. secondly, on institutions. the international institutions and international law of today were shaped and created in a completely different world. each day we realise that they are not adapted to the new challenges, new opportunities and new threats of today’s world. i believe, therefore, that the european union should support the idea of a new conference on security and cooperation in europe in a larger europe – from vancouver to shanghai, not only to vladivostok – in order to create a new space of security, of freedom and of cooperation. i think that this should be one of our top priorities, and we should not be afraid that others perhaps have other ideas on that.

in writing. the assessment of the role of the nato-eu alliance must start from the recognition that the political landscape of europe, but also of the us, has fundamentally changed in recent times, today, with the european union becoming a legitimate actor of international security. this requires the 'repoliticization' of the alliance, which must become a forum for open dialogue on the major issues in which it is to be involved. a frank transatlantic dialogue, for example, on how to deal with terrorism, is sorely needed precisely because the allies have different perspectives on how to respond to this common challenge. in the context of the increasingly diverse challenges to global security - from inter-ethnic conflicts in the immediate vicinity of allied territory, to global terrorist networks and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction - member states must attach particular importance to the process of reflection and dialogue on this issue and support the reform processes in the alliance, and i am referring in particular to security issues in the immediate neighbourhood, as the alliance can play a key role in building democratic defence and security institutions in the balkans and the wider black sea region.

since some hungarian colleagues have recently complained that their rights are not respected in romania, i would like to make a few clarifications. the approach of the election campaign should not give rise to attacks and insults against a state of law which, through its legislation, has provided an example in the field of interethnic relations. respect for minority rights is guaranteed by the constitution of romania. citizens of hungarian nationality are proportionally represented in local administrative structures, with hungarian minority parties having 195 mayors and four county council presidents, 2,684 local councillors and 108 county councillors. having a majority in the above-mentioned local and county councils, they manage local budgets at their will; this means local autonomy. at the parliamentary level, the hungarian minority has three members in the european parliament, 22 deputies and nine senators in the national parliament and has participated in the government of romania for the last twelve years. the complaints we hear are pure political election rhetoric.

in writing. in times of economic downturn, the temptation is to cut back on research funds. but i am glad that by discussing this report on the proposal for a council regulation on the community legal framework for european research infrastructures we are sending an important signal that research remains a priority for the european union. i am convinced that by establishing this institutional framework to support research activity we will see results that support the european economy. because research is not a whim, but a necessity to ensure the competitiveness of the european economy on a global scale. i want to emphasize one very important aspect where research can play an important role. in the next 25 years, urbanization is projected to take nearly 25 percent of the land out of the agricultural cycle. to compensate for the reduced acreage, we need higher productivity on smaller acreages, with less water or pesticide use. the solutions can come through research, through biotechnology, with, of course, the principle of food safety in mind. this is one more reason to support research more and to ensure a unified framework at european level.

in writing. the social economy can play a key role in the european economy, forcing a new kind of economy, based on democratic values, putting people first and supporting sustainable development. however, the social economy faces a very big obstacle: the lack of institutional visibility, caused by the fact that it is not recognized as an economic area separate from the two: public and private. we call on the commission and the member states to develop a legal framework that recognises the social economy as a third sector, to impose rules that clearly define which entities can operate in this sector, so that no other type of organisation can benefit from funding or public policies designed to encourage social economy enterprises. we also call on the commission and the member states to provide financial support, training and advice and to simplify the procedures for setting up social enterprises. in this way, the social economy will effectively fulfil its role in the overall context of the european economy by helping not only to combat poverty but also by facilitating access to the resources, rights and services needed by citizens to participate in society.

in writing. energy efficiency is one of the major objectives of the european union, and its achievement is an important step towards achieving sustainable development. therefore, alongside the effort of member states to actively engage in promoting energy efficiency policies, there must also be coordination at community level to achieve much better results. one way to achieve energy efficiency is to insulate homes. a study shows that at community level it is possible to reduce energy losses by about 27%, which implies a reduction in the costs borne by citizens. one problem faced by local communities undertaking a housing rehabilitation project is the complex process they have to follow. future measures should therefore take into account the simplification of those procedures. the energy efficiency of buildings by insulating them must also be targeted at the most disadvantaged social groups and thus lead to a strengthening of the principle of solidarity in europe.
last year the commission proposed an economic recovery plan which is proving very difficult to implement. member states and their governments need to be proactive, especially in times of crisis. member states may apply reduced vat rates to supplies of natural gas, electricity and heating or cooling, children's clothing and footwear, books, newspapers and periodicals, pharmaceuticals and medical equipment for disabled persons, and restaurant services. it just takes vision and political will. the building sector is the sector with the largest number of jobs. i strongly support the need to allow member states to apply reduced vat rates for renovation and repair works aimed at increasing energy savings and energy efficiency. as rapporteur for the directive on the energy efficiency of buildings, i have even proposed reduced vat rates for energy efficiency and renewable energy products. i support the rapporteur's proposal and believe that this measure is particularly important, especially in this period of crisis.
in writing. the european commission adopted in july 2008 a proposal on the application of reduced vat rates after 2010. the sectors concerned are in particular the so-called labour-intensive services and services provided locally to local consumers (services related to the construction/energy renovation of dwellings, personal care and catering sectors). the proposal is also part of the small business act, which aims to stimulate the more than 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises in the eu to grow the economy and create new jobs. i support this report because carefully targeted low vat rates offer specific advantages as a means of creating a tax regime that promotes jobs, increases productivity and reduces the underground economy, especially in the current context of the financial crisis. i ask the commission to monitor closely the application of these reduced vat rates in the member states in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market. congratulations to the reporter!
in writing. − by my vote in favour, i support the revision of the rules of procedure on the petitioning process as i believe that it brings about procedural improvements in the evaluation and classification of petitions. the new regulation will make petitions easier to process, thus promoting the interests of citizens. one of the important changes to the petitioning process is the emphasis on the private or confidential nature of the petition. private refers to the name and personal details of the petitioner and confidential refers to the subject matter of the petition. under the new rules, the removal of the private or confidential character, or both, is left to the discretion of the petitioner. i also consider it very important to declare petitions admissible by qualified majority, since the right to petition is a fundamental right of citizens, which is based on primary legislation and should not be restricted by a politically motivated decision. under the revised regulation, if the committee responsible fails to reach a consensus on the admissibility of a petition, it is declared admissible at the request of at least one quarter of the committee members.
in writing. − research infrastructures are playing an increasingly important role in the advancement of knowledge and technology by offering unique research services to users in different countries. it can be considered extremely important that they, by unlocking the research potential of all eu regions, will attract young people to science, thus playing a key role in building an effective research and innovation environment. in the less developed countries, however - and i am thinking here of romania - the limited resources and the complexity of technical and organisational aspects represent a major difficulty in creating european research infrastructures, and so, as these structures will only be able to develop in developed countries, we must ensure that we do not witness a new brain-drain towards these centres from within the european union.
in writing. − who statistics say that currently 450 million people experience a mental, behavioural or psychological health problem, representing 12% of the world's population. it is also said that by the year 2010, depression will become the most common disease of modern society. for example, in romania, in just one hospital, the clinical hospital of psychiatry dr. alexandru obregia, over 22,000 admissions were recorded in 2008, most of them for depression and schizophrenia. those vulnerable and marginalized groups, such as the unemployed and immigrants, but also people with disabilities or people who have suffered abuse are more prone to depression in the context of the economic crisis. all countries face a shortage of medical personnel to treat patients with mental illnesses, with the average in poor countries being 0.05 psychiatrists per 100,000 people. the problem is accentuated in many countries by the migration of specialized medical personnel. i think we will have to deal with the mental health of people in the first place with less superficiality and that all member states have to have concerted programmes to limit by all means the spread of this phenomenon.

in writing. − the directive which has just been voted represents a further step in the development and application of common rules and measures necessary to regulate the situation of immigrants, in particular third-country nationals employed illegally in the european union. the prospect of a better standard of living, generated by the possibility of finding a job, is one of the key factors encouraging illegal immigration. at the same time, the benefits to employers have the consequence of losing public funding and distorting competition in the economic sector, depriving illegal workers of social security and pension rights. that is why this directive concerns immigration policy and the sanctions are aimed at the employer and not at the third-country national. particular attention should also be paid to nationals of the new member states who, despite their status as european citizens, are still subject to transnational employment contracts, thus limiting their free access to the labour market of the old member states. measures such as the obligation for employers to examine the residence permits of third-country workers, as well as financial and criminal sanctions for employers, underline the efforts of the community and the member states to coordinate immigration and illegal labour policies. and in the context of the european union facing a sharp demographic decline, we must bear in mind that the solution is not to expel but to regulate the situation of these workers. it is with this hope that i voted for this report.
in writing. − it is well known that visa policies and strict immigration rules have never succeeded in curbing illegal migration, but have only helped to develop networks of illegal immigrant trafficking. the proposal to sanction employers who use illegal nationals is timely, but we must be careful not to make it ineffective, as the reasons why people immigrate remain the same whether or not sanctions are introduced against employers, and the proposed controls will force undocumented immigrants to choose even worse jobs with even lower wages, especially in the current economic crisis. it is clear that these measures represent only a partial and incomplete solution to illegal immigration and black labor. it is necessary that eu countries start now to have a coherent and common policy on illegal immigration.
in writing. − simplifying the issue, illegal immigrants exist for two reasons: the precarious situation in the country of origin and the demand in the labour market in other countries. if for the first problem we have the development funds and cooperation programmes supported by the eu (obviously still insufficient), for the second situation the problem has been treated differently at member state level so far. but there is a need for uniform provisions at community level to penalise employers, as this is often a transnational phenomenon, with networks of traffickers of live meat taking advantage of the vulnerability of illegal immigrants. i am glad that the problem of employers profiting from illegal immigrants has been brought to the attention of the european parliament and i am convinced that the application of this directive will improve the practice of hiring in the community. whereas previously, state policies have focused more on how to prevent illegal immigrants from entering the labor market, this time we are tackling the root of the problem. at the same time, however, this report should not be interpreted as closing the union's borders. on the contrary, we must keep the borders of the labour market open, provided that the flow of workers is legal and adapted to the needs of the state concerned.

in writing. − in security and defence, the european union's actions as a global actor have been embodied in conflict prevention interventions, giving it the status of the world's leading peace promoter. if the end of the cold war era called into question nato's role, new security threats and the progress made by europeans in defence and in conducting civil-military operations in different parts of the world demonstrate the need for a new configuration of eu-nato cooperation. in this context, the lack of a common european foreign policy, as well as disparities between member states in military funding and technological capabilities, make nato an indispensable partner in the field of military crisis management. the so-called division of labour - pesa supporting civilian operations and nato ensuring the rapid deployment of large military forces - should ensure complementarity rather than competition between the two bodies. the rapporteur's proposal to create an eu operational headquarters could therefore serve this very purpose by complementing the existing nato command structures in the field of joint civil-military operations. we must also take account of the situation in eastern europe in future eu-nato relations, and in this context it is important to promote an open door policy and to support a constructive dialogue with russia on collective security in this part of europe.

in writing. the competitiveness of smes is often undermined by barriers to cross-border trade. the removal of these barriers would bring more legal stability and allow for a more efficient calculation of the liability risks of businesses and entrepreneurs. with this report, the european parliament has shown that it fully understands the crucial role that smes play in the competitiveness of the european economy. a well-designed european private company statute, complementing existing legal forms, would benefit the competitiveness of european smes in many ways, strengthening the european internal market, simplifying the legal framework for businesses, thus reducing consultancy costs and facilitating access to cross-border markets, improving integration and economic growth. this status would also provide more flexibility for smes. smes account for more than 90% of the eu economy and two thirds of jobs. they should therefore be given the best conditions to contribute to economic growth in an integrated internal market, to seize the opportunities and to meet the challenges of globalisation.
the european asylum system is currently faced with a lack of coherence in the legal instruments on international protection. the significant differences between the decision-making processes in the 27 member states on asylum applications mean that the recognition rate of applicants for refugee status varies from 0% to around 90%. in addition, the dublin criteria disproportionately burden the member states which are the external border of the european union, as they are responsible for the treatment of asylum applications as the first country of entry. phenomena such as secondary movements from one member state to another and multiple applications continue to exist. one of the most pressing needs in european asylum policy is the exchange of analysis, experience and information between member states. practical solutions must also be found for developing cooperation between the administrations responsible for examining asylum applications. communication between member states on the different treatment of applicants for international protection according to their country of origin remains, however, the most difficult problem to solve. i hope that the regulation on the creation of a european asylum support office, proposed by the commission three weeks ago, will allow a partial solution to the current problems. i urge the future heads of this european office not to ignore cooperation with the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders, the european migration network and the competent bodies in the member states and third countries that carry out activities in the field of migration and asylum. in addition to avoiding duplication of effort, such cooperation will facilitate coordination between member states and the use of their expertise in asylum matters.
with the number of refugees worldwide increasing and the european union receiving more than half of the asylum seekers, the establishment of a common european asylum system is urgent. in this respect, the proposal to create a european asylum support office to coordinate national policies of different countries in order to avoid a disproportionate burden on certain countries is welcome. i believe that this office should be organised in such a way that it can play an important role in a crisis and assess asylum applications correctly. i believe that the new member states of the european union, romania and bulgaria, need to receive support from the european union through effective solidarity mechanisms, in order to guarantee adequate reception conditions for asylum seekers. but let us not forget that at european level we must act proactively, not reactively, by paying greater attention to cooperation with third countries in order to prevent crises.
each year, the member states of the european union take in millions of people seeking refuge from persecution and conflict in their home countries. however, at the level of these countries, the rate of recognition of refugee status ranges from 0% to 90%. moreover, the dublin system, through the process of refugee readmission in the first country of transit, creates a discrepancy between these and the central states in terms of the coordination of asylum policies and measures for refugees. as my predecessors have said, the common european asylum system must enable member states to ensure a high level of protection for refugees, from their reception to their full integration into local communities, by establishing a common asylum procedure with clear, uniform and reasonable time limits within which the authorities can deal with asylum applications. special attention should be paid to solidarity between member states in order to coordinate large flows of asylum seekers from certain countries, both through financial assistance and through the adoption of internal resettlement and relocation mechanisms, which allow for a uniform dispersal of refugees throughout the european union.

in writing. a european solution to the problems faced by roma requires that we consider them as citizens like ourselves, even if they are subject to exclusion; representative organisations and roma communities must be active actors in the development of inclusion policies. increased efforts are needed to improve housing conditions and access to education and health services; these are minimum conditions for obtaining and maintaining employment in the countries where they live; mobility opportunities have had a perverse effect on them, accentuating discrimination. women are even more vulnerable because they face multiple discrimination - gender, ethnic and social. national inclusion and poverty reduction programmes exist; the results are modest. the economic crisis should in no way be used as an excuse for not implementing social inclusion programmes; on the contrary, it is a reason for concerted action. the roma, like any other disadvantaged group, can pay dearly for the effects of the crisis. the aberrant reactions we've seen in italy are a warning. problems can be thought of as solutions or as culprits. the right has always preferred to blame others; the vulnerable, first. as a representative of the left, i prefer to find solutions.
in writing. i call on the commission to take concrete action to support the integration of roma into the labour market through measures to fund training and reform and measures to strictly enforce legislation on combating discrimination in employment. i reiterate the need to create within the ec a specialised department to ensure interaction between the commission and national governments, with a view to implementing projects aimed at the roma minority, in terms of their social, economic and cultural integration.
in writing. we are all aware that the issue of the situation of the roma is not just a national problem of each individual state, but a european problem and must be solved at this level. i would stress that the new member states in particular need real support from the eu for the integration of roma both socially and in the labour market. it is well known that the number of roma who do not have access to the labour market in the european union is worrying and we must not delay the creation of effective european programmes that stimulate first of all the access of roma to education, so that this phenomenon of unemployment is not perpetuated from generation to generation. the free movement now enjoyed by roma in the new member states did not mean that they could also access the eu labour market as easily, and we can say that roma migrants to other member states have only exported their own poverty. in the context of the economic crisis, roma citizens have even more difficult access to the labour market, which means that a large proportion of them live below the poverty line. it is therefore a major challenge for us, in a time of economic crisis, to encourage employers to provide jobs for the largest minority in europe.
vice-president of the commission. - madam president, the commission welcomes this own-initiative report by the european parliament. it pays tribute to the work undertaken by the imco committee and by you, madam, as its rapporteur, and it welcomes in particular the study carried out on questions of integrity. as my colleague mr mccreevy has pointed out in his previous speeches, the approaches currently adopted in the member states are too different to allow for a legislative initiative. the latest discussions in the competitiveness council made it clear that member states would not agree on such an initiative. the treaty also provides a number of guiding principles. the case law of the court of justice has recently confirmed, in the placanica judgment of march 2007, that sports betting activities do constitute services within the meaning of article 49 of the treaty. member states have the right to legislate in the field of gambling at national level. if they wish to restrict gambling activities, it is up to them to carry out the necessary studies to justify these restrictions, for example, in terms of addiction or fraud. where such measures are proved necessary, the treaty requires that they be taken in a non-discriminatory manner in respect of national operators and operators established in other member states. the commission intends to fulfil its duty by investigating any complaint submitted to it and will initiate infringement proceedings if it is found that infringements of the treaty have been committed. it is encouraging to note that following the infringement proceedings initiated, a number of member states, such as france, hungary and italy, have approached the commission and started to amend their legislation. the commission is, of course, trying to help the member states to find solutions to respond to infringement procedures. the commission published a study on the legal and economic aspects of the gambling market in 2006. in these circumstances, the commission does not consider it necessary at present to play an increased role in carrying out studies relating to national legislation or to the wider problem of addiction, fraud or other wrongdoing. however, this report provides some particularly useful insights.
the reporter. − i would first like to thank the european commission for the welcome green paper initiative on agricultural product quality and for the consultation launched on this subject. the green paper responds to a real need in the member states to promote the image of agricultural products, especially their quality advantages, to european and non-european consumers. these high standards are demanded by consumers and are a way of achieving maximum added value. although the co-decision procedure does not apply, i hope that the opinion of the european parliament will be clearly taken into account in the following stages. i would also like to thank my colleagues on the committee on agriculture and in particular the experts for their support in promoting this report. simplifying marketing rules, better informing consumers, especially about the origin of food products, and better protecting european quality products internationally are some of the most important proposals in the report. quality policy cannot be dissociated from the future of the common agricultural policy and from challenges such as climate change, the need to conserve biodiversity, energy supply and water management. at the same time, consumers - we all know - are increasingly interested not only in food safety but also in the origin and production methods of food. certification schemes are associated in the consumer's mind with the guarantee of superior quality. the aim of standards should be to help farmers deliver products of a quality that meets consumer expectations, does not disappoint consumers and facilitates price comparisons for different product qualities. as rapporteur, i want to reduce the complexity of the european system of basic standards and the many provisions that european farmers have to comply with. i am in favour of simplification and the adoption of rules which sufficiently guarantee european food safety. i also propose ways of simplifying the standard-setting process by shortening procedures within the commission, by transferring this task to other bodies or by referring to international standards. i also believe that simplification must take account of the administrative burden on public authorities or stakeholders. as market requirements change and technology advances, marketing standards may become partly outdated and need to be adapted and updated. the european union must insist that all foodstuffs comply with production standards, especially those relating to hygiene and safety. the european union must also ensure that its own products compete on an equal footing with those of third countries. i am in favour of the mandatory indication of the place of production of primary products, by mentioning 'product made in the european union' or 'produced outside the european union'. i also want to extend this system to processed food products, which take account of the origin of the main ingredients and raw materials and which establish a link between the place of origin and the place of final processing of the product. it considers that rules should be adopted on the use of the terms 'mountain' and 'insular' as this will add significant value to agricultural products and foodstuffs from these disadvantaged regions.
vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs petre, for this report. the european policy on the quality of agricultural products is a major challenge for farmers, the food chain in general and, of course, consumers. this is why the commission adopted the green paper on the quality of agricultural products and consulted stakeholders before making legislative proposals. the commission, mrs petre, welcomes your report and the discussions that have taken place in the various committees of the european parliament. these discussions were in addition to the 560 contributions received during the consultation period to help the commission to define strategic guidelines which will be set out in a communication due at the end of may this year. the commission intends to help european farmers to communicate the demanding production conditions they comply with. i have noticed that the proposal to indicate the place of production has received very little support, and even less so the idea of a european logo indicating compliance with european standards. on the other hand, there is a demand for the labelling 'country of origin'. the commission welcomes the support for its approach to simplification of marketing standards. the commission has always been in favour of simplifying legislation where necessary; so, mrs petre, you encourage us, you encourage us to continue our work. the commission took note of the request to define optional reserved terms such as 'farmer' or 'mountain'. i can tell you that this is also the view of a majority of those who responded to the green paper. as regards geographical indications, the commission shares your view. the procedures should be simplified or at least accelerated. we are currently looking at how to go through all the answers that have been given in the green paper. the question of an agency remains open. however, the pros and cons of such an organism will have to be carefully studied. as regards the wto negotiations, i can assure you that the recognition of european quality systems remains firmly on the commission's agenda. there seems to be a consensus on the need to harmonise and regulate certification systems and to achieve mutual recognition between these systems. guidelines could be sufficient and would allow us to avoid too much red tape. this is the first step towards a genuine policy on the quality of agricultural products. the commission is now looking forward to the next steps and the fruitful discussions that await us, and mrs fischer boel, my colleague, assures you through my voice that the commission will involve parliament in all the next actions it will undertake in this field, which you have rightly stressed, mrs petre, the importance of, not only for producers but also for all of us consumers.
in writing. – in a highly globalised world, farmers face increasing pressure. in order to be competitive, they can either cut costs or specialise in production of niche high-quality products. thus, food-quality schemes do not only provide consumers authentic products but can also support rural development. to give farmers an alternative for rural development, we need to simplify the marketing standards and strengthen the incentives for small-scale producers to participate. but simplifying standards does not mean less quality or authenticity. eu standards for placing food on the market are already among the toughest in the world. to preserve confidence in quality schemes, it is necessary to implement them with reinforced controls and traceability systems. furthermore, in the case of ‘protected geographical indications’ or ‘protected designation of origin’, it would be desirable to label the main ingredient(s) with the place of origin if not from that particular area. consumers identify in these products specific qualities resulting from a certain origin or farming method. there are, however, cases when the ingredient indicated on the label is not exactly the same as the one really used in the food, for example ‘parma ham’ not really coming from parma.
in writing. the report by mr reul is extremely important in the context of the current economic crisis and the challenges of climate change. as a member of the committee on agriculture, i have always argued that we should not underestimate the importance of investments in clean technologies and renewable energy as solutions to reduce dependence on oil, reduce carbon emissions, but not least as a solution to create new jobs and stimulate economic growth. i appreciate that biofuels are also listed in this report as an under-exploited resource and i hope that the recommendation to facilitate market access for biofuels will be taken into account by the european commission. the use of biofuels is an economically and socially viable alternative for rural development and environmental protection. at the same time, i welcome the increased attention paid to energy efficiency in buildings, which is a priority in the european economic recovery plan and is mentioned in mr reul's report as a solution to reducing the demand for fossil energy resources. energy efficiency has the added benefit of reducing the burden of bills on consumers, as the economic crisis is increasingly affecting them.

in writing. i welcome both the integrated approach (the synthesis of seven separate industrial emissions directives into one text) and the tightening of implementation to use the best available techniques to innovate in cleaner production. developing less polluting products involves the participation of different actors such as businesses, competent authorities and ngos. the directive provides opportunities for cooperation between the different parties (local authorities and businesses), which allows them to stimulate innovation. there are good examples of this in the netherlands and denmark, as well as in eastern european countries for example in romania. the proposed single industrial emissions directive, together with all the options recommended in the strategy package, will improve the ability of the legislation to achieve its environmental and health protection objectives in the most efficient and cost-effective way possible, while ensuring that unnecessary administrative costs are reduced (with an estimated net reduction of eur 105-225 million/year) and that distortions of competition within the eu are minimised, without affecting the competitiveness of european industry.
in writing. while industrial activities play a fundamental role in maintaining and increasing economic well-being, we must not lose sight of their impact on the environment. the review of the ippc directive on integrated pollution prevention and control has placed a great deal of emphasis on the setting of limit values for certain combustion plants and the use of existing best techniques, so-called bat, to ensure a sufficient level of environmental protection. i supported the introduction, as from 1 january 2020, of a limit value of 350 g of carbon dioxide for combustion plants producing electricity of more than 500 mw, as these plants lead to an increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere and, by implication, to an increase in global warming. the introduction of a limit value would act as an incentive for investment in emission reduction techniques, with all installations to comply with this limit value by 2025. i believe that reducing pollution from various industrial sources will help the european union to achieve its objective of keeping the global temperature below 2 degrees celsius, and the effectiveness of this directive will be reflected in the inspections to be carried out on all combustion plants and in compliance with the conditions of authorisation.

in writing. − given the importance of free movement in the european project, the measures taken over time have been aimed at liberalising internal border controls. however, these steps must be accompanied by measures to strengthen controls at the external borders. given that, for example, up to 8 million illegal immigrants were registered in the eu in 2006, i consider the commission's initiative to introduce an entry-exit system, a registered traveller programme and an electronic traveller authorisation system in the period 2012-2015 to be a necessary initiative. the european borderless area, transformed from a dream into a reality, can only work if we assume a common responsibility and show solidarity in managing the eu's external borders, an action in which the eu's border states, including romania, will play an important role. however, we must not lose sight of the fact that border protection systems such as eurosur and frontex already exist and it is essential for their functionality to assess to what extent the new initiative can complement them without creating the risk of overlap. in addition, our concern must be to respect the right to privacy of individuals, but also to develop new, less invasive technologies.
