on behalf of the ppe-de group. this report is the product of collaboration between the members of this forum. i would therefore like to thank my colleagues, and in particular mr lambrinidis, but also mrs gacek, mr alvaro, mrs segelström and mr mavrommatis, with whom i had the pleasure of working, more as a shadow rapporteur. i believe that the report covers the main themes of interest on strengthening security and fundamental human rights on the internet, referring to the protection of rights stipulated by the specific regulations in force in their digital dimension, as well as to the recognition and development of new principles of internet governance. the text strikes a good balance between the protection of freedom of expression and privacy and the need to continue the fight against information crime cybercrime and also highlights the important issue of excessive surveillance of internet activity, which can degenerate into a new form of censorship. it addresses issues relating to the educational dimension of the internet, e-learning, the definition of digital identity, and the recognition of the user's right to the content he or she posts on the internet and the protection of personal data, in the sense of giving the user the possibility to permanently delete his or her own content. these are sensitive issues in the current context, where social networks are increasingly populated by young people, and not only. that is why i have urged my colleagues to vote for this report with all their convictions.
today, the internet has reached a new stage as an indispensable tool for business, but also as a global forum for the expression of diverse opinions. however, this development has generated ambivalent positions. on the one hand, the internet continues to offer fabulous opportunities as a catalyst for educational, cultural, economic and social development, and on the other, it is perceived as a platform that can be used to promote violent behaviour that undermines people's freedom and security. furthermore, the internet's global nature has also made it a threat to privacy, with citizens' online activities often subject to surveillance by governments, law enforcement authorities, companies, and even criminals and terrorists, to the point of identity theft. in this context, the legal line that separates the security and fundamental freedoms of citizens on the internet from unlimited monitoring by various authorities must be identified, so that legislation becomes effective, and not excessive, in the fight against crime. it is therefore necessary to define global standards on data protection, security and freedom of expression through sustained cooperation between internet operators and internet users. it is also important and in this respect i fully support the rapporteur to examine and set limits on the consent that users, whether governments or private companies, may be required to give up part of their privacy in order to benefit from certain services or privileges on the internet. last but not least, mr president, i believe that the member states must make efforts to align national legislation on the protection of fundamental rights on the internet, which can also help to shape a common strategy to combat cybercrime or cyberterrorism. my congratulations to mr lambrinidis and the entire team who contributed to this report.

(the president of the council is here) − the committee on the internal market and consumer protection has formulated its position on the basis of the fact that the negative effects of an infringement of antitrust law are very often felt economically at the end of the commercial chain, affecting final consumers and small businesses. in this case, the compensation for the damage suffered is important but at the same time difficult to obtain, since there are many victims and small amounts. i therefore called for the adoption of a package of legislative and non-legislative measures to be the instrument through which all european citizens affected can defend their right to fair and full compensation. we support all measures designed to remove the difficulties in achieving this objective: facilitating access to documents, reducing the costs of judicial proceedings and reversing the burden of proof. we welcome the commission's proposal to combine representative actions brought by qualified entities with collective actions with explicit consent. however, we believe that collective opt-out actions should remain under discussion given the advantage they represent: a final solution and a reduction of uncertainty.
on behalf of the ppe-de group. although the ec treaty clearly prohibits cartels and other breaches of competition law, it is still difficult for affected consumers in the european community to recover their compensation rights. in romania, for example, a cartel formed in the cement industry was recently fined several million euros. however, the legislation in force does not oblige the competition authorities to be involved in compensating victims. i would like to stress the need for these authorities to take into account the compensation paid or to be paid when calculating the fines imposed on undertakings guilty of abuses, so that there is no gap between the damage caused and the punitive measures, and especially to ensure compensation for those affected by such practices. i therefore welcome the commission's intention to improve the way in which the rights of consumers affected by infringements of the law are guaranteed throughout europe. parliament has been very clear that there should be no opt-out system in europe. therefore, victims must be identified as soon as possible at the time of a complaint. the 'opt-in' system ensures that victims of the infringement of competition law will indeed be compensated. parliament wants no one else, whether lawyers, trade associations or the consumer protection, to benefit from private actions. i also think that parliament is introducing an important new element which the commission's proposal has omitted. alternative dispute resolution mechanisms are in many cases much more effective for victims who are entitled to compensation than judicial procedures and i am referring to the fact that when seeking compensation, out-of-court settlements must be initiated in the first place. they are much less costly than private actions and consumers will be compensated for damages suffered much more quickly.

madam president, obviously there are two schools of thought in this house when it comes to russia, reflecting the ambivalent attitude of the member states. in essence, it is not about russia – because many agree that this power is inevitably a strategic partner of ours – but about how to respond to her behaviour, which does not always conform to our standards. thus, while the first school suggests keeping russia accountable for every departure from those standards – and obviously mr onyszkiewicz’s report is in this category – the second school is more accommodating, motivated primarily by pragmatism. the question is, therefore, which of these two attitudes ensures better management of our common issues (economics, trade, energy, security, research and education), satisfying our interests while avoiding abdicating our own standards. which one will have more impact on russia’s behaviour? although i personally am sceptical about anybody’s capacity to really influence russia’s behaviour one way or another, i still plead for an eu position combining pragmatism with integrity. in the end, although this report is nominally about russia, in reality it concerns us too.

according to the universal declaration of human rights and the convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, all citizens have equal rights and freedoms, enjoy equal protection of the law without distinction of race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or any other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth, social status or any other circumstance. but i would like to stress that decisive and effective action against all forms of discrimination is needed, since discrimination in europe is still strong and affects the most diverse strata of society. in many cases, it is not enough to prohibit discrimination of any kind, but it is also essential to take various positive measures, for example in the case of people with disabilities. many countries - to name just a few: italy, france, finland and spain - have also taken positive measures to grant autonomy to traditional national minorities. the european union and its member states have an obligation to ensure that citizens are treated equally in their rights and in their treatment, even in an institutional form. there is a need for independent institutions at european level to monitor and guarantee that states do not only commit themselves theoretically to the principle of equal treatment, but also take concrete measures to ensure the effective application of this directive.

reporting for the opinion of the committee on employment and social affairs. - the financial crisis has imposed much more prudent lending policies, which are necessary for banks but destructive for the economy. the negative effects are felt in the real economy, especially in smes and public authorities. these projects aim to increase social and regional cohesion, create jobs, exploit local resources, and facilitate entry and re-entry into the labour market. the normally large common budget is now an indispensable source of funding to stop the negative effects from multiplying. the commission is therefore proposing to simplify the rules and speed up access to the structural funds and the european social fund. for countries less experienced in accessing funds, the advantage is twofold. we consider it necessary and welcome that the european financial institutions intervene in the financing arrangements, modify the structure of eligible expenditure, and eliminate the ceilings on advance payments or advance approval. however, access to funds is not an end in itself. the financial impact is over eur 6.3 billion. the sum is considerable. as representatives of the public, we want the funds to achieve the objectives for which they were created. we're writing a blank check today and demanding the necessary transparency in the spending of money. we're also hoping to set a positive precedent. in the past, many initiatives, especially social ones, have been rejected on the grounds that they lack a legal basis. the amendment of this regulation proves, if necessary, that where there is political will, there is also a legal basis. let's not forget that.
on behalf of the ppe-de group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank mrs garcia perez for her report. cohesion policy reforms are very important and aim to mitigate the negative effects of the financial crisis. the flexibility allowed in the distribution of community funds will provide national economies with immediate liquidity to enable investment in the real economy. their effect will be immediate, and the first results will certainly be seen in the months to come. the european commission is supporting member states' economies through four major priorities, the most important of which are: increasing pre-financing from the erdf and the european social fund and support from the european investment bank and the european investment fund. in 2009, prefinancing, which is mainly for the new member states, can thus help to overcome the crisis and achieve social and territorial cohesion. the report on the eligibility of energy efficiency and renewable energy investments in housing should also be given high priority. the thermal rehabilitation of dwellings should be high on the european union's agenda in view of the added value of this measure. with the rising costs of thermal energy, member states need to include energy efficiency projects in their crisis programmes. they bring important benefits to both the economy and the population, such as: injecting liquidity into the economy as well as creating jobs, reducing thermal energy costs, protecting the environment by reducing greenhouse gas emissions, ensuring social cohesion and supporting low-income families. in romania, it is estimated that 1.4 million apartments are in urgent need of investment for rehabilitation.
i would like to welcome the idea of these coordinated measures at the beginning of my speech and to thank the rapporteurs in particular for the work they have done. we all know what the effects of the crisis are in each of our countries, from reduced growth and job prospects to rising budget deficits and recession. european cohesion policy can be an equally credible and effective instrument in this context. europe, as we know, is deeply affected by the crisis and it is encouraging that the union was able to react so quickly to find solutions. the decision to amend the regulations of existing funds, which have already proven their effectiveness, is the most appropriate. the creation of a specific crisis response fund would have been a far too long procedure. simplifying the eligibility criteria for expenditure, increasing pre-financing from the erdf and the european social fund and speeding up major project spending are measures that they hope will help member states emerge from the economic and financial crisis. in parallel with the economic crisis, europe is also experiencing an energy crisis. the measure that allows the regional development fund to be used for investments in energy efficiency and renewable energy in housing will, in my view, have a big impact. romania, like other countries in central and eastern europe, is familiar with many problems related to multi-storey housing. the old buildings are extremely poorly insulated and the inhabitants are largely unable to insulate their homes themselves. we hope that this will help european citizens to save energy, both in their pockets and in the face of global warming. the current romanian government has established this measure as a priority level 0 measure and the facilities that have been adopted allow this priority to be already secured.
2010 is the year in which we will make the mid-term review of the use of the structural funds and i believe that energy efficiency must be a priority. i regret that no amendments to these reports have been accepted. as rapporteur for energy efficiency in buildings i proposed to increase by up to 15% the share of the erdf that can be used for energy efficiency in buildings. it is actually about more flexibility and it is up to the member states to decide whether and how much they want to allocate to this area. i understand the urgency; the eu-15 countries must be able to use the structural funds for energy efficiency and i believe that this will allow for the exchange of good practice and support for the new member states. i ask the commission to come forward by 30 june 2010 with a new legislative proposal to raise the maximum ceiling to 15% or even to have a minimum threshold of 10% of the erdf quota for energy efficiency in buildings.
in writing. the wider european economic recovery plan, namely the revision of the european regional development fund (erdf) regulation, presents a number of opportunities for eu member states, all the more so as the international economic crisis is slowing down national economies. the new measure proposed in the review report of the erdf regulation on investments in energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy in the housing sector for all member states is beneficial in terms of both job creation and improving the energy efficiency of housing. meeting the objectives of the community's energy and climate change strategy is a very serious matter, which should not be overlooked by the economic crisis or other considerations. in this respect, the proposals for the revision of the erdf effectively combine measures to counter the effects of the economic crisis (by creating jobs, increasing investment, etc.) with measures to protect the environment (by insulating buildings and investing in renewable energy). for these reasons, i believe that the energy efficiency and renewable energy in housing investment report is an important step the union is taking and i am confident that member states will make the most of this opportunity.
in writing. the social consequences of the crisis are increasingly felt in all member states. in particular, as regards employment, we are facing a situation which is deteriorating rapidly in all the member states of the european union. the secretary general of the organization for economic cooperation and development points out that the unemployment rate in the eu and the us is estimated to reach 10% this year. this is a worrying increase, given that the average rate in the eu was 8% in january. in romania, although the official rate is below the european average, there has been a 1% increase in the unemployment rate in the last year, reaching 5.3%. but we expect accelerated growth as more businesses are forced to lay off workers and as our nationals working abroad return home because of job losses. that is why, in view of this situation which threatens to degenerate into a cascade of social imbalances which we risk losing control over, i would like to stress the need to pay greater attention to the problems of unemployment, which are the most affected and vulnerable among us in the context of this crisis.
in writing. i welcome the commission's proposal to amend the erdf regulation so that all member states and regions in the european union can invest in energy efficiency and renewable energy measures in housing with the help of the structural funds. under the current regulation, the erdf already supports interventions in the housing sector, including energy efficiency, but only for the new member states (eu-12) and under certain conditions. it is important to allow member states to change their priorities and reprogram their operational programmes to finance measures in this area if they wish. given that a ceiling of 4% of the total erdf allocation to each member state has been imposed on expenditure related to improving energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy in existing dwellings, it is necessary to increase this ceiling to 15% so that investments in this area have the greatest impact on european union citizens. in conclusion, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr emmanouil angelakas, on his contribution to this report.
in writing. according to research, electricity consumption in romania is one of the highest in central and eastern europe. improving energy management could be a direct driver of economic growth, reducing pollution and saving resources so that they are used in the most productive way. to achieve this in romania, it is necessary to inform the population about the economic benefits that can be obtained through energy efficiency management practices, providing to this end, to all those interested, advice on access to erdf funds on modern energy saving techniques. this will increase the comfort of household consumers, while reducing energy bills, increasing energy efficiency throughout the energy chain and verifying compliance with current energy efficiency legislation. this will decisively lead to a reorientation of energy policy based on energy production towards an active energy policy of energy saving, aiming at saving resources through energy conservation.

the community code on visas integrates the procedures and conditions for the issuing of schengen visas by the member states and harmonises the existing provisions on decisions to refuse, extend or annul such visas. it is important that a member state which does not have its own consulate in a third country is represented by another member state which has a diplomatic or consular representation in the third country. the code should take into account the bilateral agreements concluded by the community, in particular with the states participating in the european union's neighbourhood and partnership policy, with a view to facilitating the processing of visa applications and the application of simplified procedures. i do not think that the right of member states to cooperate with commercial intermediaries will make a significant contribution to simplifying the procedures for processing visa applications. this is because the code provides for the presentation of visa applicants in person when submitting the first application for biometric data, as well as the possibility for any visa applicant to be called for an interview for a schengen visa. the purpose of the schengen visa code is to provide a uniform external image of the european union, to treat visa applicants equally, and to create clear criteria and rules for exemption for a number of third countries. in this context, i think it is appropriate to recall that the european union must do everything necessary to ensure that its member states are treated uniformly by third countries which apply visa exemptions only to certain member states. it is not possible to have two classes of european citizens when they want to travel to, say, australia or the united states.

second package of measures to adapt the technical specifications on the chronotachograph is currently being discussed in committee. these measures will make it easier for drivers to use the tachograph has been a success. the commission, together with the member states, has just convinced the countries that are joining the aetr to adopt these new rules from 2010. but of course the member states must ensure that social rules are applied in a harmonised way in europe. i was able to say this to parliament on behalf of the commission and i shall listen carefully to the speeches of the various on behalf of the pse group. european regulations on working time and driving time, rest periods for road hauliers are concerned with social conditions in road transport, but above all with road safety. unfortunately, the european union has failed to do enough to reduce road accidents. it is true that member states must improve their traffic controls. as rapporteur on social conditions, i analysed the first report by the european commission, which was supposed to be biannual; unfortunately, it was delayed then, but in that report i found that some member states had exceeded the minimum number of checks they had to carry out, but there were also member states which had not fulfilled these obligations. i am glad that in mr grosch's report on market access we were able, together with the council of the european union, to introduce a compromise text, namely that we requested that all traffic controls be non-discriminatory on the basis of neither nationality nor the country of residence of the transport operator. commissioner, we need secure parking areas! there was a draft report on the construction of secure car parks on the border between the european union and russia, but unfortunately these car parks are insufficient. member states need to invest more in safe parking places because, unfortunately, 40% of robberies of road hauliers take place in parking places. i also made an amendment to the budget so that we could allocate a sum for the construction of safe parking lots. i believe that the conditions regarding driving time and rest periods can only be met if we create conditions for transport operators to comply with these provisions.
respect for driving times and rest periods for drivers is essential to ensure a high level of safety on european roads and to protect passengers. the european commission adopted in january 2009 a package of measures to prevent misuse of the tachograph and to strengthen member states' controls on compliance with driving and rest regulations. the measures are welcome in view of the many problems that have been raised over time with working time recording systems, primarily those related to the digital tachograph, and the fact that the existing legislative provisions have been considered to be inflexible and difficult to apply. i consider that one of the most important aspects to be considered by the commission is the value of the transposition of directive 22/2006 into the national laws of the member states and the harmonisation of the national provisions drawn up pursuant to article 19 of regulation no 561/2006. in these respects, romania has fulfilled its obligations, but there are still member states where this process is not definitive, which also results in difficulties in the correct application of sanctions in cross-border situations and in the collection of fines for breaches of legislation. in view of the biennial reports of the member states in this last reference period, and the many difficulties reported by the carriers, i call on the european commission to consider the appropriateness of revising regulation no 561/2006.

rapporteur. − mr president, of all the fundamental rights granted to eu citizens, the one that helps unite all of us the most is the right of freedom of movement in the european union. that right, provided for in the treaties, is implemented by directive 2004/38/ec, which lays down both the conditions and the restrictions for eu citizens and their family members to move and reside freely within the territory of the eu. as of 1 january 2006, over 8 million eu citizens have exercised this right to reside in another member state, and millions more have used it to travel through the eu. as the european parliament rapporteur on the evaluation of this directive, i must say that the concrete application of the right of free movement for our citizens is seriously undermined by member states which erect dams in breach of the treaties and of the directive. first, talking about the transposition by member states, we can say it has been poor at best. the commission, along with two separate studies commissioned by parliament, points to a series of problems, some of them being breaches of the core rights of eu citizens. these problems are highlighted in my report. there are many unjustified administrative burdens, particularly for third-country-national family members, which include: entry requirements and lengthy procedural delays; a lack of recognition of free movement rights for certain registered partners, including those in same-sex relationships; public policy exceptions to serve economic or security aims which ignore the principle of proportionality, resulting in abuses of expulsion orders; and discrimination against certain nationals and ethnic communities in relation to the rights they should be granted by the directive. second, to those who chose to focus solely on abuses and misuses of this right, i agree that these issues are important, but i say that article 35 of the directive already provides member states with the possibility to fight against those abuses, such as marriages of convenience or fraud – one just has to implement it. i also want to mention that i have constructively cooperated with national parliaments, the commission and the committee on legal affairs rapporteur, monica frassoni, who all share my concern over the aforementioned transposition problems and the need for all parties to help to resolve them immediately. my report also calls for a number of measures aimed at providing solutions. one of the most important and immediate steps that must be taken is the creation by the commission of comprehensive transposition guidelines. those guidelines would serve to provide clarity in the interpretation of such notions as ‘sufficient resources’ and ‘public security’. once this has been done, it will be up to the member states to implement those guidelines, preferably by the end of 2009. discriminatory transitional agreements that restrict the movement of workers from member states that joined the eu after 2004 must finally be repealed or revised. more funding must be allocated to help local integration measures for eu citizens residing in other member states and, finally, the commission must not hesitate to open infringement proceedings against member states who are not complying with the directive. we have to recognise that member states need finally to correctly apply and transpose the directive so that these and other problems are resolved expediently. they should not try to escape their duties in ensuring free movement by asking for a revision to water down the directive. the european parliament firmly opposes such revision and thanks the commission for doing the same. it is time for the member states and the council to ensure that europe is a place where not only capital, services and goods, but also our citizens, can circulate. without free movement, there is no europe. let me conclude by saying that i shall move a revised oral amendment to a footnote in my report in order to take away any excuse for those who oppose free movement on a nationalistic, racist or xenophobic basis, but who do not dare to declare it openly, to vote against my report. with the roll-call vote tomorrow, we will see who supports europe and european citizenship, free movement and citizens’ rights without discrimination, and who does not.
in writing. i fully support ms valean's report on the application of directive 2004/38/ec, especially as recent events in certain member states have drawn attention to the flagrant violation of one of the four fundamental freedoms, namely the right of citizens to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. the inefficient or even the lack of transposition of this directive into the national legislation of the member states has also given rise to a number of abuses in the area of administrative formalities and restrictive interpretation of the legislative provisions on the concept of 'illegal residence', culminating in the unjust detention and expulsion of european citizens. however, the solution is not to close borders, but rather to look for concrete measures to facilitate the integration of citizens into the diversity of european societies. i believe that this report will make a significant contribution to monitoring the transposition of the rules laid down in this directive if the member states and the commission succeed in working together and cooperating in this respect. today, all european citizens want to live in a european union where fundamental values such as the free movement of persons are respected, but we must not forget that to achieve this goal, we all have to make our own contribution.

in writing. the eco-label is voluntary and aims to promote the spread of products with high efficiency and low environmental impact throughout their life cycle at european level. the experience gained from implementing this certification for almost a decade - 26 product categories, 622 licences and over 3000 products and services (detergents, paper, clothing, footwear, textiles, tourism, camping products) - suggests the need for more decisive intervention to address certain key aspects of the system. as many economic operators are dissatisfied with the long approval procedure for criteria and their rapid moral wear and tear once approved, changes have been introduced to their approval (maximum 180 days between the completion of the evaluation and approval, a simplified and shortened review procedure for non-essential changes to the criteria) and a new label award system. the credibility of the eco-label certification system requires:- the general principle of consumer health and environmental protection to be applied even to labelled products; - promotion activities: improving consumer information, launching awareness campaigns to maintain confidence in the eco-label, using european funds; - giving special attention to smes. i support the report and congratulate the rapporteur.

rule is that they will no longer be necessary if shareholders are able to download and list the documents, but member states may provide that companies make these documents available at their offices for consultation. another important compromise is the date for implementation of the directive, which will be 30 june 2011, as proposed by the commission. member states will also be able to decide on the consequences of temporary disruption of internet access due to technical problems. a substantial change concerns mergers and simplified divisions, when assemblies will no longer be needed for their approval. these simplified procedures alone are estimated to save around eur 154 million each year, so it is worth adopting this directive at first reading.

rapporteur. − madam president, it was quite interesting listening to all the speeches this morning in parliament at a time not only when we are living through the toughest financial and economic crisis, but also when the european elections are approaching. the reports which we have discussed today, and will vote on tomorrow, are not meant to solve the financial crisis, but we hope they will help us avoid making the same mistakes in future, or at least major mistakes, and hopefully they will support a relaunch of the european economy. when one hears that small enterprises today have to spend 10 times more than big companies in order to comply with eu legislation on reporting requirements, it is normal to wonder why this is so and how we have come to have rules which through their effects may actually kill these small enterprises and why it has taken us so long to change this. i am glad that commissioner mccreevy mentioned that company law is probably the toughest in the eu acquis communautaire. maybe it is time to change it, certainly not to make it softer, but perhaps to bring it more in line with the current realities we are living through. if we want to be more efficient, it is better to put our energy into being constructive, and i think it is fair to say that what happened with the package we discussed today is proof of this. it is proof that we have acted responsibly and we have reached a compromise with the council and the commission in order to adopt this package at first reading. can we do more? certainly, but let us vote on this and work in the right direction.
in writing. i do not want to discuss the importance of rating agencies here: everyone knows that they are vital for the rationale of an investment decision, whether it concerns financial products or issuers (and are therefore more than just opinions). but i would like to stress the importance of establishing a european agency. in a time of deep economic crisis, such as the one we are currently experiencing, the rating agencies should remain, regardless of economic conditions, transparent and trustworthy instruments that can help navigate these troubled times. we cannot hide the fact that the current crisis is also due to the rating agencies, because they have analysed classic instruments with other hybrids, against the backdrop of accusations of lack of transparency and conflict of interest. we need new presences in this field, leading to a competition in achieving objective ratings. we need to think about investor protection, about investor confidence in the ratings agencies. the union must be a guarantor of the fact that credit rating agencies operate on the basis of clear regulation. what better way to fulfil these conditions than to set up a european credit rating agency, which operates in accordance with community regulations.

in writing. − it is recognised that the use of pesticides poses a threat to both human health and the environment. the 'thematic strategy on the sustainable use of pesticides' aims to reduce the risks to human health and the environment from the use of pesticides. harmonisation of environmental protection requirements and conformity assessment procedures for technical equipment for pesticide application is a necessary condition for achieving the same level of environmental protection throughout the eu, for ensuring fair competition between producers and for facilitating the free movement of such products within the community. the correct design and construction of these equipment plays a significant role in reducing the negative impact of pesticides on human health and the environment. assuming that the average life of a pesticide sprayer is 12 to 15 years, it is estimated that approximately 125 000 to 250 000 new sprayers are purchased in the community each year. due to their higher efficiency, sprayers complying with the new environmental requirements consume less pesticide and reduce losses during mixing, loading, spraying and cleaning operations, resulting in savings for users that will offset any increase in the price of certain spraying equipment. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the new regulation introduces preventive mechanisms and price transparency for data roaming services, so that citizens/customers can better understand how to charge, control their spending and avoid the so-called 'bill shock'. the setting of caps for voice and sms roaming services and the adoption of transparency measures, as well as the preventive mechanism introduced for wholesale data charges, maintain the freedom of operators to compete in the market and to differentiate their offers within the limits of the imposed caps. this ensures that small new businesses can cope with the excessive wholesale charges of the large operators. current billing practices for voice roaming calls charged on the basis of 60-second units represent a hidden cost for consumers, which adds to a typical euro-voice roaming bill approximately 24% for calls made and 19% for calls received. the regulation should provide a sufficient level of consumer protection, allow consumers to make appropriate use of data roaming services and should not impose burdens on telecommunications operators.

brought this type of problem to the attention of the moldovan authorities on several occasions before the elections. in particular, the lack of media freedom and the persecution of the opposition by need for consistent and ambitious measures to strengthen democratic norms and institutions in moldova. enhanced eu assistance will be needed to support institution building, including judicial and police reform, and to ensure freedom and pluralism of the media. the agreement of the moldovan political parties on how to overcome the current crisis should include a commitment to thorough reforms in the above areas. in conclusion, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to stress that for many years moldova has been one of the most advanced countries in the eastern european neighbourhood in terms path. the eastern partnership will provide a new and ambitious framework for strengthening eu assistance for political and economic reform in moldova and other countries in the region. it is in the interest of all of us to ensure that democracy in moldova is strengthened and that moldova continues to move closer to the european union.

rapporteur. − mr president, i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs for their cooperation in reaching the compromise agreement with the council on the recast of the eco-design directive. it has been a challenging process, mainly due to the very restrictive nature of the recast. a legislative proposal where parliament can hardly change anything is not the appropriate framework for codecision. we are no longer an institution limited to giving assent and this is not the way parliament wants to work with the recast in the future. however, i am pleased that despite these challenges we managed to reach a compromise that confirms the basic principles of the commission’s proposal, such as the extension of the scope to energy-related products, but also brings more clarifications and more emphasis on all relevant environmental parameters. thus, the compromise improves the definition of ‘energy-related products’ by clarifying which products could be covered by implementing measures, such as window-insulation materials or some water-using products like showerheads or taps. and i insist on the fact that giving these examples does not mean that these products will be covered automatically. first, they will be subject to specific impact assessment, and implementing measures will be developed only for those products that have significant environmental impact, have significant potential for improvement and are not covered by other legislation that can achieve the same objectives more quickly and with less expense. then, the compromise provides for the assessment of the methodology used for preparing the implementing measures to better cover resource efficiency and the life-cycle approach. in times of narrowing natural resources, we must not only aim at energy efficiency but at optimising the use of resources as a whole. furthermore, we must try to reduce the environmental impact of our products not only during their use phase, but also through their entire life cycle, from raw-material selection to manufacturing, packaging, use and end of life. even if for now the directive is extended only to energy-related products, we should be prepared for a further extension to all products in the future. both the committee on the environment and the committee on industry have demanded a clear commitment to extend the scope of the directive beyond energy-related products after its review in 2012. in response, the commission committed itself to adopting the current methodology, if needed, with a view to a further extension of the scope to all products. but we could not have any firm commitment for an extension of the scope to all products after the review of the directive in 2012. i would have liked the commission to have had a firmer and more visionary approach, especially since we have all the instruments on the table today and this was the best option identified by the impact assessment. in this sense, i believe we missed the opportunity to do more for the environment with less bureaucracy. there is also the review in 2012. we will certainly not contest the fact that we need to change our consumption and production patterns by switching to cleaner products. change is needed, but change is also possible without overburdening companies and households. by building a low-carbon and resource-efficient economy we can give a new impetus to competitiveness. the eco-design directive represents a big opportunity for industry to build more competitive businesses based on green technologies. it creates a level playing field across europe, reducing red tape and production costs. it also provides flexibility for the industry, as self-regulation measures can be recognised as alternatives to regulatory implementing measures. last but not least, relevant stakeholders are consulted and associated in defining and reviewing the implementing measures and assessing self-regulatory measures. from my consultations with stakeholders, i realise that forward-thinking businesses do not wait for regulations in order to become compliant, but take proactive measures. some do it out of altruism but most do it because eco-consciousness is simply good for business. however, we need to give the industry the right signals. even though my vision of extending eco-design requirements to all products is not shared by all my colleagues, i strongly believe that only by shifting to cleaner goods can we stop environmental degradation. more than 80% of all environmental impacts of a product are determined during product design. an improved product design would avoid waste and provide consumers with more efficient, more reliable and longer-lasting products. extending the eco-design requirements to energy-related products such as windows or water taps is the first step towards a more ambitious approach and a sustainable product policy at eu level. sometimes even small steps can lead to big achievements. i hope you will endorse this compromise agreement as a way forward and you will continue keeping up the pressure to optimise the full potential for environmental improvement and stimulate the design of eco-friendlier products.
vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the commission has already made a number of proposals. i would like to begin by thanking the rapporteur, mr csibi, for his excellent work on this proposal and i am very pleased that his work has made it possible to reach an agreement at first reading. the content of the proposal is from a purely legal point of view limited. it essentially extends the scope of the existing ecodesign directive on energy-related products currently covered to all energy-related products. the commission has already made a number of proposals. it is an important step towards the third industrial revolution in europe, towards the transformation of our european economies into low-carbon economies. i have a vision of what the european product of the future should look like. the european product of the future, marked by a made in europe, looks like it is the most innovative, the safest and at the same time the most energy-efficient and resource-saving product. i am convinced that european leadership in energy efficiency and resource efficiency is not only good for the environment but also for jobs. environmentally friendly products and processes are booming today, even in the crisis. and that will continue. the directive is a good example of an integrated product policy in my view. it has worked in the past, and we are seeing good results when it comes to products powered by energy. the directive creates a framework for setting ecodesign requirements which take account of the actual environmental impact of a product throughout its life cycle. it limits public requirements to those products where significant savings potentials can be realised in an economically viable way. the current directive is already making a major contribution to achieving european reduction targets, for example by phasing out lamps, boilers and many other low-energy consumer goods. the extension of the scope to all energy-related products has significant potential for further reducing energy consumption and thus co2 emissions. to repeat, all products relevant to energy consumption are now covered by the directive. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be allowed to apply the principle of the free movement of goods in the context of the internal market. for example, requirements can now be set for products that use water, or requirements can be set for windows. let me give you an example. increasing the proportion of double-glazed windows alone can bring about 30% additional energy savings by 2020. that would mean a saving of 55,000 gigawatt hours. that's the equivalent of 27 megatons of co2 saved, or the power of two or three nuclear power plants. this shows the enormous impact of such seemingly small changes. the commission will continue its ongoing work on the 25 or so implementing measures for the ecodesign directive listed in its work programme for 2009-2011. it will also, by 21 october 2011, after consulting the ecodesign consultation forum, determine the products to be included in the second work programme, as provided for in article 16 of the directive. by 2012, the commission also intends to examine, in accordance with article 21, whether it is appropriate to extend the scope of the directive to include products that are not relevant to energy consumption but to conservation of resources. as agreed in the negotiations leading to the agreement at first reading, the commission is to make a statement. the statement is known to parliament. i shall hand them over to the bureau after this meeting. the rapid adoption of the proposal at first reading will enable the commission to implement the sustainable industrial policy and to start working on further concrete steps to save energy and reduce co2 emissions without losing time. in conclusion, let me say that the close cooperation between parliament, the council and the commission has accelerated the negotiations. i am very pleased to say that the commission can accept all the amendments tabled by the rapporteur, mr csibi. thank you. thank you.
vice-president of the commission. - ladies and gentlemen! the controversy in this debate is not about energy efficiency. i think everyone agreed that the commission's proposal will lead to a major step forward in improving energy efficiency, saving energy and thus reducing greenhouse gases. that is the point of this proposal. this is a proposal in the context of our climate and energy policy. i am a little surprised at the very wide-ranging criticism i have just heard. i think i have made it quite clear in what i have said here that the integrated product policy which the commission is pursuing links energy efficiency and conservation of resources. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. that seems to have been overlooked. i would therefore point out that, in the case of implementing measures, the annex 1 directive already covers all environmental characteristics throughout the life cycle of the product - including resource efficiency and not only energy efficiency - and that the commission takes these factors into account when determining the ecodesign parameters to be regulated in the implementing measures, using a methodology specifically developed for the ecodesign of energy-based products. so the question of resource efficiency is central to the actual implementation measures. but let me say this about the politics of this issue in general: i think that this new product policy, which will have a huge impact on consumer behaviour, on all industrial production, on our entire economic structure, cannot be done in one go, but we must do it step by step. it is also wise to wait until we have a minimum of experience to legislate, and we are completely lacking this experience at the moment in the area of resource efficiency in normal consumer products. but we have made it clear where we are going and i am quite sure that the next time we look at this directive, the focus will no longer be on energy efficiency but on conservation of resources. i would be very grateful if, in the present situation, we could do what is reasonably possible today; if we could do together now what really makes a significant, sustainable contribution to reducing energy consumption and thus to achieving our goal of making europe the world leader in energy efficiency and co2 reduction. the commission's statement on the csibi report (a6-0096/2009) is as follows: the commission declares that adoption of the proposed extension of the directive of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for the setting of ecodesign requirements for energy-related products will not affect the implementation of the work programme currently established. moreover, the commission will take due account of the experience gained under the directive when establishing the work programme and proposing new implementing measures under the recast directive. in line with article 15 (2) (c) of the directive and the principles of better regulation, the commission will in particular strive to ensure that overall consistency in eu legislation on products is maintained. in addition, the commission will, when assessing the appropriateness of extending the scope of the directive to non-energy related products in accordance with article 21, consider the need for adapting the methodology for identifying and addressing significant environmental parameters for such products.
rapporteur. − mr president, compromise is never easy, and today’s debate showed us that we have different opinions, but it is also never easy to find a good middle way between the progressiveness of the european parliament and the realism of the dgs and the council. but i would like to sincerely thank our colleagues from the dgs for their flexibility. i would also like to thank commissioner verheugen for his support and kind words, and the shadow rapporteurs who helped me in this legislative process. from my point of view i think that we have succeeded in finding a good middle way in this proposal and in finding a way of dealing with this package which will not overburden european industry but also will help us attain a more energy-efficient and resource-efficient european industry. but i would also like to echo to some extent what my colleague mr krahmer said, and to express my hope that the implementation of this proposal will be as quick as our legislative work. so i would like to see quick implementation, i would like to see quick results and i would like to see results which first of all serve the interests of european citizens, and then also those of european industry.
in writing. the current financial crisis only reinforces the eu's responsibility to honour its energy and environmental commitments. many measures (e.g. eco-design) are needed to make the way we consume and produce in europe more sustainable, without imposing additional costs on businesses and citizens. eco-design addresses the first stage in the product life cycle. the new concept aims to 'eliminate the environmental impact from the product and the production process'. about 80% of the environmental impact and life-cycle costs of a product can be determined in the design phase. the accumulation and dissemination of knowledge generated in the eco-design effort of manufacturers is one of the key benefits of the reform of the ecodesign directive. informing consumers about energy and resource efficiency should become a key element in their decisions. improving energy efficiency is the fastest and least expensive way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. an accessible database is needed to increase transparency for consumers, industry and competent authorities and to facilitate the rapid collection of data for consumers and smes. i support the commission's call to create a public eco-design database available online.
in writing. as the european union has recognised in the sixth community environment action programme that there is a need for a more substantial reduction in the environmental and health impacts of pesticides, the regulation on statistics on plant protection products fills the gaps in the use of pesticides in the member states. the data provided by the commission on the use and sales of pesticides have shown that there is a need for a harmonised methodology at community level for the collection of statistical data, both at the stage of placing products on the market and from producers. we are all aware of the need to establish a more coherent legislative framework at european union level in the field of pesticide use. i would therefore stress that it is desirable to establish a common framework for the systematic production of community statistics on the placing on the market and use of pesticides in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity.

author. - one of the problems affecting the justice systems of many countries in the world is not so much the lack of a well-developed legal framework as the lack of implementation of the decisions taken by the judiciary. in countries affected by the scourge of civil wars, permanent conflict or massacres, the consequences are disastrous from the humanitarian and development point of view. in the case of the special court for sierra leone, it is all the more important that the court decisions be implemented, since this court sets a number of important precedents in international law. it is not only the first court of its kind established in the same country where the events were tried, but also the first to indict and convict, in the person of charles taylor, the former president of liberia, an african head of state still in office at the time of the trial's inception. these elements, together with the recent conviction of three former rebel leaders from the civil war era, are strong signals of the will of the international community and the government of sierra leone to fight hard against the sense of impunity that has been evident among those who have committed atrocities for a decade. the international community must complete the proposed project to strengthen the rule of law and justice in sierra leone. the court's mandate is due to expire in 2010, and the government of sierra leone has been explicit about its inability to enforce the sentences. it is therefore essential that the european union and its international partners active in the peace process support and support the implementation of the judgments issued by the special court. not only does progress towards peace and stability in the region depend on this, but also the credibility of the special courts set up with the support of the international community in other countries.

for recasting the energy labelling directive, intending to bring further benefits to european citizens, industry and public authorities alike, firstly by extending its scope to all energy-related products, secondly by strengthening market surveillance, and thirdly by encouraging energy-efficient public procurement and incentive practices. i am very grateful to the rapporteur, mrs podimata, for producing, in a short period of time, the report on a highly complex proposal, giving the opportunity for a second-reading agreement, when the council will really enter into the discussion. i would
