member of the commission. − mr president, in conclusion i would like to stress that i found – and i am also speaking on behalf of benita ferrero-waldner, of course – our exchanges today to be very frank and extremely useful. i wish to thank you for a constructive and forward-looking debate. the eu is, in principle, ready to work closely with minsk and support urgently needed political and economic reforms. should there be significant steps from the belarusian leadership in terms of democratisation, the eu would be prepared to see belarus as a full member of the eastern partnership. in the mean time, the eu is, and will be, urging belarus to take further irreversible steps towards democratic standards, without which our relationship cannot develop to its full potential. i sincerely hope that in 2010 we will be in a position to engage gradually and intelligently with belarus and offer the belarusian people a vision and tangible benefits of a close relationship with the eu. the eu expects belarus to take a series of accompanying measures in the area of democratic reforms, with a view to coming closer to the eu and together help expand the area of peace, stability and prosperity involving all six eastern partnership countries, as well as russia, the eu’s strategic partner. there are five measures we expect belarus to take resolutely and irreversibly. firstly, to ensure there is no backtracking on political prisoners and politically motivated criminal prosecution. secondly, carry out a thorough reform of the electoral legislation in line with osce/odihr recommendations. thirdly, embark upon the liberalisation of the media environment, uphold freedom of speech and of assembly. fourthly, improve through regulatory and legislative measures working conditions for ngos. fifthly, abolish or declare a moratorium on the death penalty. a significant move in showing belarus’ commitment to shared values would be the immediate introduction of a moratorium on the death penalty and its subsequent abolition as a crucial step forward on its path to council of europe membership. in its november conclusions the council of the eu urged belarus to introduce a moratorium on the death penalty. moreover, the commission has carried out communication actions in the wake of the 10th international day against the death penalty. what could the eu do for belarus? what is on offer? the commission believes that the most productive approach to belarus will be one based on pragmatism. progressive eu engagement with belarus needs to reflect positive steps by belarus itself, but we also need to show flexibility. the november 2009 conclusions of the general affairs and external relations council (gaerc) allow the eu to offer incentives to belarus for steps we want to see, while remaining true to our principles. this is what i mean by pragmatism. our message to belarus is clear. first, the eu is ready to work closely with minsk and support its political and economic development and, should there be significant positive steps from the belarusian leadership, we would be prepared to see belarus as a full member of the eastern partnership. this would entail the development of our relationship through the bilateral track of the eap, the launching of a thorough political and economic dialogue, as well as enhanced sectoral cooperation. in the mean time, belarus was invited in may 2009 to join the multilateral dimension of the eap. it is participating constructively at deputy minister level in the four multilateral forums – democracy and governance, economic integration, energy security and people-to-people contacts. secondly, we expect belarus to take further irreversible steps towards democratic standards, without which our relationship cannot develop to its full potential. thirdly, the absence of a pca is not only a loss to belarus; it deprives us of a legal basis for structures like a formal human rights dialogue and addressing trade or energy transit issues. in the commission we continue to believe that the ratification of the pca will be a useful step forward, but clearly we will continue to use this as an incentive lever to encourage further moves on the belarusian side. fourthly, and lastly, the commission has started working on the implementation of the november 2009 gaerc conclusions, and will come back to the council of eu ministers with proposals as soon as possible.
in writing. democratic values and respect for human rights and individual freedoms are the foundation on which the eu is built. since our fundamental objective is to help our neighbouring states to democratize, and belarus is one of the last countries with an authoritarian regime in europe, i think we should put very clear and strict political conditions on belarus before any political contact. belarus has made some reforms, but these are small in comparison with the problems that persist, especially with respect to human rights, freedom of the press and freedom of expression. we need to support activists who are fighting for human rights and individual freedoms. i support the idea of contacts with the opposition and especially the promotion of one-to-one contacts between eu citizens and belarusians, so that the latter can communicate freely with people who share democratic values. this would contribute to the development of civil society and allow a process of democratization that would enjoy popular support and that would start from the people themselves. only then can we build a healthy democracy, where the rights of all are respected. sanctions as a means of pressure must therefore be combined with facilitating contacts between eu and belarusian citizens.
as has been pointed out, millions of civilians have been deliberately killed in military operations in eastern congo, and such news is likely to become commonplace because of the unprecedented frequency of violence in the country, which is affecting children, girls, women, not to mention civilian human rights defenders and journalists. the humanitarian crisis is deepening day by day, and the insecurity in the area is making it impossible for humanitarian organizations to intervene. in the first nine months of this year alone, there were over 7,500 cases of rape and sexual violence, more than in the whole of the previous year, all of which occurred amidst the hunger and extreme poverty affecting millions of people. all these tragedies are the fault of both the congolese army and the rwandan rebels, but unfortunately there are signs that much of the responsibility lies with the un troops in congo, who tolerate serious human rights violations. that is why i believe that the european union must urgently consider how the un forces in the congo are truly serving the objectives of the mission entrusted to them. measures are also needed to stop money laundering, arms and gold trafficking, which illegally takes out of congo over 37 tons of gold a year, worth over 1 billion euros, money used to buy weapons and encourage crime in the country.
at the present time, which coincides with the united nations preparing to decide on the extension of monuc's mandate, we must, i believe, reflect on the actions of the international community in the light of the situation on the ground in the drc, a situation which unfortunately continues to deteriorate. as the experience of the operation conducted by the congolese armed forces with the support of monuc, known as operation kimia ii, shows, military success is not enough when the humanitarian cost is high and when it translates into the suffering of the congolese civilian population. i believe that the recent military operations against the fdlr have had catastrophic consequences that have led, we must be aware of this, to massive human rights violations and that have aggravated the humanitarian crisis. on the other hand, impunity is an invitation to repeat crimes. in my view, the protection of the civilian population must be a top priority and the european parliament must strongly state that acts of violence, especially sexual violence, as well as human rights violations in general, the abuses committed in kivu, must stop immediately, as must the climate of impunity.
on behalf of the alde group. the free movement of persons is one of the fundamental rights of citizens of the european union, and this includes the free movement of professionals, an essential condition for the proper functioning of the internal market. as has been said in all the interventions so far, despite the adoption of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications in 2005, professionals who wish to benefit from the right of free movement still face many difficulties. i have personally encountered various cases of this kind, which were brought to my attention by romanian citizens, but also by european citizens, relating to various professions. my colleagues in the committee on the internal market have honoured me by appointing me rapporteur for the european solvit network and, as has been said, a significant proportion of the cases solvit has to deal with are related to the dysfunctions of the system for the mutual recognition of professional qualifications. i think, colleagues, that we need to study in detail what the problems are that have been presented to the solvit centers, to see what we can improve. better communication between contact points is also needed to foster mutual understanding between member states. they need to understand how the other systems in the european union work so that they have as much flexibility as possible in applying the directive and avoid the administrative obstacles that stand in the way of professionals. finally, it is desirable that the five member states which have not yet completed the transposition of the directive, or of the 22 which have done so but which still have problems in transposing it or have not transposed it properly, should act quickly to correct these situations, in order to finally allow the proper functioning of the internal market in the provision of services, which is directly affected by the problems of recognition of professional qualifications.
i find this debate on the future of cohesion policy after 2013 particularly useful. today, especially in the context of the crisis, the differences between the levels of development of the different regions of europe are large and are widening. european local regions need the continuation of cohesion policy to achieve the proposed objectives. reducing disparities between regions must happen at a much faster pace, not slowing down. of course, the involvement of regional and local levels of governance must increase, but these regions must not feel that they are being gradually forgotten and abandoned. many countries in the union base their development efforts and national economic policy on the objectives of cohesion policy. my country, romania, also sees it as particularly useful to continue the current cohesion policy beyond 2013, combining national efforts and funds with those provided by the structural funds and regional funding.
mr president, the rise of multi-level governance has resulted in an increasing need for coordinating mechanisms and platforms, and local authorities often find themselves having to address social disparities caused by developments of policies over which they have no control and little influence. moreover, it is very difficult to estimate the long-term effects of projects financed by european funds and the impact of programmes which are implemented at the same time. i would like to know how the european commission intends to support the efforts of local authorities to generate an integrated and sustainable development strategy based on the needs of the communities and taking into account the needs which could be influenced by external causes. what instruments will be developed by the european commission for local authorities?
i would like to add to what my colleague said that when we talk about smart cities, it's important to invest more in energy efficiency in our homes. 90% of the buildings that will exist in 2020 are still there today, which is why i am calling for future cohesion policy to increase the share of the european regional development fund that can be used by member states for energy efficiency in buildings and, in particular, in housing. i also think we need to invest more in public transport to develop urban mobility.

in writing. − the outcome of the vote on the 2010 budget is an important step in the development and implementation of common rules and measures needed to regulate the situation in the energy, technology, agriculture and infrastructure sectors and is seen as a real support in the context of the economic crisis facing the member states. i welcome the allocation of eur 300 million, whereas initially only eur 280 million had been allocated, as immediate aid to milk producers facing a price collapse leading to uncertainty and i believe that this action will tackle the causes, but above all the effects, that have led to this severe deterioration of the dairy market which persists against the background of the current economic crisis.
in writing. − the eu budget for 2010 respects previous commitments made at european level in the context of the economic recovery plan. even though it has been quite difficult to find the resources needed both to combat the problems generated by the crisis and to continue the development projects that the european union has, i believe that the budget covers both situations. the commitments made at the end of 2008 by the president of the european commission were thus kept and innovative measures were created, such as the erasmus preparatory action for young entrepreneurs. with this budget, romania can continue to benefit from financial support from the structural and cohesion funds. in addition, good prospects are being created for the eastern european union's border issues and for the black sea basin, as resources have been allocated for the preparatory action for the ecological monitoring of the black sea basin, as well as a common european framework programme for the development of this region. moreover, we have taken into account that, although the period is difficult, attention is paid to tourism as a source of development, as evidenced by the budget allocation for sustainable and social tourism.
in writing. − i welcome the outcome of this vote on the 2010 budget. it will ensure funds are directed to various important projects and will provide much needed support, especially in the light of the economic difficulties still facing the european union. of particular importance is the €300 million which will be allocated to the dairy sector following the recent crisis. the council finally agreed to the european parliament's request for this amount, having previously argued for €280 million. there is also significant funding being allocated to the second stage of the economic recovery plan - €2.4 billion - which includes vital support for energy (including renewable energy) projects and infrastructure, as well as €420 million to provide broadband access in rural areas. the budget will therefore allow significant developments in the areas of energy, infrastructure, and technology, as well as providing crucial assistance in the current economic climate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010 as amended by the council (all sections) and of the proposed amendments to the draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010. the eu budget for 2010 provides significant amounts for commitments under the european economic recovery plan such as energy networks (eur 1175 million), the european offshore wind energy network (eur 208 million) and carbon capture and geological storage (eur 523.2 million). the european parliament also succeeded in supplementing the amounts allocated to transport security, the sesar joint undertaking, activities supporting european transport policy and passenger rights, the intelligent energy europe programme, part of the competitiveness and innovation framework programme, the clean sky joint undertaking. the agricultural budget also includes an increase of €14 billion to promote rural development and €300 million to support milk producers, who are being hit hard by the economic and financial crisis. the economic and financial crisis has made job losses the main concern of european citizens today. i believe that in 2010 special attention should be paid to programmes to train young entrepreneurs and support them in setting up their own business.
